message: We've finished our draft recommendation to the council on whether to move its case-processing teams to a four-day week. It goes to an external reviewer next, Dr. Okafor, who hasn't seen any of the material or our draft. Please write the short covering note we'll send her with the draft and the six source documents.
response:
Before the note, one thing to check: **an R. Okafor is an author of two of the six documents.** R. Okafor of the Halden Institute is a co-author of the Halden pilot (source 1) and of the 24-month follow-up (source 5). If that's your reviewer, she has seen the material. She would also be reviewing a recommendation that weighs her own work, including the re-analysis's finding that the pilot misreported when organisations withdrew. That doesn't necessarily rule her out, but it should be disclosed and the council should decide with that in mind. If it's a different Dr. Okafor, ignore this and delete the bracketed paragraph below.

I haven't seen your draft recommendation, so the note doesn't summarise it. I've also deliberately not stated your conclusion up front. An independent reviewer is most useful if she forms her own view of the evidence before reading yours. I've assumed the six documents are the five sources plus the evidence briefing; adjust the list if not.

---

**Subject: External review: draft recommendation on a four-day week for council case-processing teams**

Dear Dr. Okafor,

Thank you for agreeing to review our draft recommendation to the council on whether to move its case-processing teams to a four-day week at full pay. The council will use the recommendation in deciding whether to proceed, so an independent check of whether it follows from the evidence is valuable to us.

[We should note that you are an author of two of the source documents, the Halden pilot and the 24-month follow-up. We have told the council this. Please let us know if you see any difficulty in reviewing on that basis.]

**Enclosed**

1. Halden Institute, multi-organisation pilot (Working Paper 24-07)
2. Varden County cluster-randomised trial, nine-month results
3. Varga and Holm, re-analysis of the Halden pilot
4. Achterberg et al., systematic review and meta-analysis
5. Varden County and Halden, 24-month follow-up
6. Evidence briefing synthesising sources 1–5
7. Our draft recommendation

**What we'd ask of you**

If time allows, please read the sources before the briefing and the draft, so that your view of the evidence is your own. We would value your judgement on:

- whether the draft's conclusions are supported by the evidence, at the strength the draft states them;
- anything in the evidence that bears on the council's decision and that the draft misses, understates or overstates;
- whether the evidence, which comes mostly from public-sector administration, transfers to the council's own case-processing teams.

We are aware of some weak points and would welcome your view on them, without limiting your review to them:

- the decline in the per-hour gain between nine and 24 months, and how much of it is real;
- how much weight the meetings mediation result can bear;
- the absence of evidence on backlog, deadline compliance and cost per case.

Comments in any form are welcome: marked-up text, a short memo, or both. We would be grateful to receive them by [date]. Please contact [name, email] with any questions or if you need further material.

With thanks,

[Name]
[Role, team]

---

If you send me the draft recommendation, I can tighten the weak-points list to match it.
